h1: Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 — A Calm Urban Retreat in Bang Khen at an Honest Price
intro: If you picture a resort and instinctively think of the sea or mountains, this one asks you to rethink. Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 tucks itself into a quiet dead-end lane off Soi Raminthra 23 in Bang Khen — a pocket of calm that feels far removed from Bangkok's traffic noise, yet puts you within walking distance of the Pink Line BTS at Lat Phrao station (around 470 metres). Twenty-four rooms, free parking, complimentary bicycles for guests, and a private balcony on every room. Rates start from approximately ฿700–฿1,200 per night — the kind of value that circulates quietly among people who know this part of northern Bangkok well.

body.html: Leelawadee Resotel is a small Thai hotel group with several Bangkok properties. The Raminthra 23 branch sits deep inside a lane that buffers it from the traffic on the main Raminthra Road — and that positioning is the point. What guest reviews note first is the quiet: the kind of stillness where you hear birds in the morning rather than truck engines. The cleanliness score of 8.7 on Trip.com (noticeably higher than the property's overall 7.8) tells you the rooms are genuinely well-kept — not merely described as clean.

The 24 rooms divide between Superior Twin and Superior Queen configurations, each measuring around 22.5 square metres. Every room comes with air conditioning, flat-screen TV, refrigerator, electric kettle, a private en-suite bathroom with shower, free Wi-Fi, and a private balcony — the outdoor space is one of the most frequently praised features in reviews, and it's what earns the resort framing rather than just "budget hotel." Some rooms also have a larger terrace, worth requesting if you plan to spend quiet mornings outside.
"Beautiful and clean, peaceful. Not far from the BTS at all — about 250 metres — and a 7-Eleven is 100 metres away. Excellent value."

Bang Khen's Raminthra corridor is consistently underrated by tourists but genuinely useful for those who know it. Pink Line BTS Lat Phrao station is approximately 470 metres away — around 5 to 7 minutes on foot — giving you a direct connection to the MRT interchange at Ratchadaphisek and onward to the Sukhumvit/Asok business core. Don Mueang Airport (DMK) is 10.5 km away, roughly 20–25 minutes by taxi or Grab. Wat Phra Sri Mahathat, the striking pagoda-memorial complex, is about 5 minutes by car. Central Ramintra and Krirk University are within easy reach, as is Ying Charoen Market at Saphan Mai.

Two amenities stand out above the price point: free bicycles for guests and a shared terrace lounge. The bikes are useful for exploring the lanes around Raminthra 23 — the neighbourhood has a residential character that rewards slow exploration at pedal speed, especially in the cooler morning hours. Free on-site parking adds to the appeal for guests arriving by car from the expressway or from Don Mueang.

Honesty requires noting a few things reviews surface: the location is a double-edged sword. The quiet lane that makes the property peaceful is also a lane that puts you further from conveniences. Getting to restaurants, shops, or the main road requires a short walk or ride rather than stepping straight out. Staff communication in English has limits — multiple reviews note this, though it's more an inconvenience than a barrier given that translation apps handle most situations. And one or two reviews mention a faint odour in the lobby area, worth checking in current reviews before booking.

For a starting rate of approximately ฿700–฿1,200 per night — which buys a clean private-balcony room with free parking and free bikes in Bangkok's northern corridor — Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 sits in a distinct niche. It suits travellers who actively want the quiet rather than tolerating it, who are comfortable navigating a residential area, and who'll use the BTS as their primary route into the city. It's less suited to guests who want dining, a pool, or shopping within a two-minute walk.

honestSummary: Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 is a clean, genuinely quiet urban retreat that delivers more character than the price suggests — private balconies, free bicycles, and a garden atmosphere are real differentiators. The trade-off is a lane location that requires more intentional planning around meals and transport. Know what you're choosing, and it delivers well.
honestChecks: If you need restaurants, cafes or a convenience store at your doorstep — the end-of-lane setting means a short bike or walk to get there. A 7-Eleven is 100 metres away, but sit-down dining requires a bit more effort. Consider Petchsiri or Gems Park if immediate street-level access matters more.

If you don't speak Thai and rely heavily on hotel staff for help — English communication at the front desk is limited. Come prepared with a translation app and confirm key details (early check-in, requests) via the OTA booking platform in advance.

If you need a pool, on-site restaurant, or resort-scale facilities — this is a 24-room property focused on clean rooms and a calm setting. There is no pool and no in-house dining. It works for travellers who eat out; less so for those who want everything on-property.

tips.title: Grab the Free Bike First Thing
tips.body: Borrow one of the hotel's complimentary bicycles and explore Soi Raminthra 23 and its connecting lanes in the morning cool. It's also the easiest way to reach the 7-Eleven and local food stalls without calling a Grab for a 200-metre errand.

tips.title: Use the Pink Line as Your Main Route
tips.body: Lat Phrao station (Pink Line BTS) is a 5–7 minute walk. Change to the MRT at Ratchadaphisek to reach Asok, Sukhumvit, or Chatuchak without sitting in traffic. This line makes the hotel's location far more practical than it looks on a map.

tips.title: Book Your Don Mueang Grab the Night Before
tips.body: Don Mueang Airport is 10.5 km away — about 20 minutes in normal traffic. If your flight departs before 6 AM, pre-schedule a Grab via the app the evening before; surge pricing and driver availability at 3–4 AM can be unpredictable.

tips.title: Plan Your Meals Before You Arrive
tips.body: The hotel has no in-house restaurant. A 7-Eleven is 100 metres away and local Thai food shops open from around 7 AM in the soi. For more variety, Central Ramintra and Ying Charoen Market at Saphan Mai are 10–15 minutes by taxi or bike.

faqTitle: FAQ — Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23, Bang Khen Bangkok

faq.q: Where exactly is Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 and how close is the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 11 Soi Raminthra 23, Junction 8, Anusawari, Bang Khen, Bangkok 10220. The nearest BTS is Lat Phrao station on the Pink Line, approximately 470 metres away — a 5–7 minute walk. From Lat Phrao you can interchange to the MRT and reach central Bangkok destinations. Don Mueang Airport (DMK) is 10.5 km away, about 20–25 minutes by taxi.

faq.q: What are the room rates at Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿700–฿800 per night for a Superior Twin or Queen Room (22.5 sqm). Prices can rise to ฿1,000–฿1,200 during public holidays and peak travel periods. Always compare across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com to find the current best rate.

faq.q: Does Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 really offer free bikes and parking?
faq.a: Yes — both free on-site parking and complimentary bicycles are available for guests. The bikes are particularly useful for reaching the nearest convenience store (100 m) and exploring the neighbourhood without calling a ride. Parking is on-site and well-suited for guests arriving by car.

faq.q: Who is Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23 best suited for?
faq.a: It suits travellers who value quietness and value for money over central location: business visitors with meetings in the Raminthra/Bang Khen corridor, passengers with Don Mueang flights, and anyone who wants a clean, calm base in north Bangkok while using the Pink BTS Line to move around the city. Less ideal for first-time Bangkok tourists who need restaurant and nightlife options on the doorstep.

faq.q: Is there a restaurant or pool at Leelawadee Resotel Raminthra 23?
faq.a: No restaurant and no swimming pool. There is a shared terrace/lounge area. A 7-Eleven is 100 metres away, and local Thai food shops operate in the surrounding lanes from early morning. For more dining options, Central Ramintra mall and Ying Charoen Market at Saphan Mai are both 10–15 minutes away.
